name: ASA (Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate)
chemical_makeup: Terpolymer of acrylonitrile, styrene, and acrylate rubber — ABS chemistry with the butadiene rubber replaced by UV-stable acrylate
summary: The outdoor workhorse: ABS-like strength and temperature resistance with strong UV stability. Needs an enclosure and ventilation. Example entry pending Phase A research.

drying.dryness_validation: No popping or surface pitting; consistent gloss on a test print

storage.recommendations: Sealed with desiccant; less moisture-critical than PETG/PA but dry storage improves surfaces

compatibility.notes: HIPS dissolves in limonene, giving soluble supports for styrenics

plate_recommendations.notes: Clean textured PEI at 100 °C; glue stick as release/adhesion tuner on large flats

emissions.notes: Styrene is a respiratory irritant and possible carcinogen with chronic exposure. Print enclosed with exhaust or HEPA+activated-carbon filtration; never in occupied unventilated rooms.

safety_notes: Enclosure serves double duty: warp control and emission containment

sources: EXAMPLE ENTRY — values are typical published figures; replace via Phase A research
